meta.title: Top 100 Hyrox Athletes to Follow 2026
meta.subtitle: The racers and voices defining fitness racing — ranked. World champions, Elite 15 regulars, doubles stars, and the creators teaching the sport.

scoreModel.name: Hyrox Follow Score
scoreModel.gate: Two tiers on one scale. Elite — races elite heats and podiums at majors, scored results-first. Creators — coaches and media voices who may race sub-elite but shape how the sport is trained and watched.
scoreModel.notes: Reach is log-scaled and recomputed from researched follower counts. The five judgment factors — results, content, momentum, crossover, longevity — are calibrated across research segments so no category is scored on an easier curve. Counts marked verified were browser-checked at the listed date; the rest are approximate.

meta.disclaimer: Rosters and results move fast in Hyrox; the ranking is reviewed monthly against the current season. Educational and editorial — inclusion is not an endorsement.

entries.name: Lauren Weeks
entries.who: American Hyrox pioneer and three-time World Champion (2020, 2021, 2023), still ranked world No. 1 in 2026.
entries.why: The most decorated racer in the sport's history and the benchmark every Elite 15 season is measured against.
entries.takeaway: Build a training approach that holds up across years, not just one peak season.

entries.name: Jake Dearden
entries.who: 247 Gym head coach and Red Bull athlete; Men's Doubles World Champion 2024, Elite 15 regular with a 49:07 PB at EMEA London 2026.
entries.why: Follow him for polished high-performance training content and race breakdowns from someone who still races Elite 15 himself.
entries.takeaway: Keep racing yourself even after you start coaching — it keeps your advice honest.

entries.name: Hunter McIntyre
entries.who: American Elite 15 racer, three-time HYROX World Champion (2020, 2022, 2023) and former OCR/CrossFit Games competitor.
entries.why: The sport's biggest crossover name — still winning Pro titles in 2026 and the athlete non-Hyrox fans have actually heard of.
entries.reach: IG follower count not independently verified this session (approx, unverified 2026)
entries.takeaway: Bring skills from other disciplines, like OCR or CrossFit, into training instead of specializing narrow.

entries.name: Alexander Rončević
entries.who: Austrian Elite 15 world-record holder in singles who, with Tim Wenisch, won the 2026 Stockholm Doubles World Championship and set the Men's Pro Doubles world record (47:40) in London.
entries.why: The most dominant all-around men's racer in the sport right now, singles and doubles both.
entries.takeaway: Train doubles and singles both — the crossover skills sharpen each other.

entries.name: Joanna Wietrzyk
entries.who: Australia's fastest Hyrox woman; 2025 World Championship runner-up and multiple major-race winner.
entries.why: A consistent podium threat with a growing sponsor roster including Puma and Amazfit.
entries.takeaway: Chase consistency over one big result — repeat podiums beat a single win.

entries.name: Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr
entries.who: Eight-time CrossFit Fittest Woman on Earth who now races Hyrox mixed doubles, pairing with husband Shane Orr and with CrossFit star James Newbury.
entries.why: The most decorated CrossFitter alive racing Hyrox doubles brings the whole CrossFit fanbase along with her.
entries.takeaway: Pair with a doubles partner whose strengths cover your weak stations.

entries.name: Tim Wenisch
entries.who: German Elite 15 racer who swept singles and Pro Doubles at the 2025 Chicago Worlds, then took the 2026 Stockholm Doubles title and the Men's Pro Doubles world record with Alexander Rončević.
entries.why: The most decorated men's doubles racer active right now, and only 26.
entries.takeaway: Race both singles and doubles in the same season to build all-around fitness.

entries.name: Dylan Scott
entries.who: American Elite 15 racer, the 2026 HYROX World Champion after a chaotic wall-ball finish in Stockholm.
entries.why: The reigning world champion right now — his 2025 bronze-to-2026 gold arc is the story of the season.
entries.takeaway: Drill your finishing station so a close race doesn't slip away late.

entries.name: Jake Williamson
entries.who: British men's open doubles world-record holder (47:57 with Fabi Eisenlauer, Berlin 2025); Puma-sponsored, part of Instagram's Athletes for Purpose roster.
entries.why: Follow for the record-breaking doubles racing and for an openly gay athlete pushing HYROX toward a wider, more inclusive audience.
entries.takeaway: Find a doubles partner whose pace matches yours exactly — mismatched pairs lose time.

entries.name: Linda Meier
entries.who: Reigning 2025 Hyrox World Champion (58:56), a German IT specialist turned Elite 15 racer.
entries.why: The athlete who just took the world title heading into her title defense in Stockholm.
entries.takeaway: Treat Hyrox as a serious second discipline alongside your day job — a title doesn't require training full-time.

entries.name: Meg Martin
entries.who: Australian Elite 15 doubles racer; with Calypso Sheridan holds the women's doubles world record (53:21) and placed 5th at the 2026 World Championships.
entries.why: A record-setting doubles specialist whose M3GA brand and run clubs reach well beyond the racecourse.
entries.takeaway: Commit to one fixed doubles partner and drill pacing together toward a target time.

entries.name: James Kelly
entries.who: Australia's fastest HYROX athlete, Elite 15 racer, 4th at the 2025 World Championships and part of Australia's winning 2026 relay team.
entries.why: One of the most consistent vloggers in the sport — weekly training breakdowns make him a go-to for how to actually train.
entries.takeaway: Document your own training weekly — the habit of review builds skill faster than random workouts.

entries.name: Camilla Massa
entries.who: Captain of Italy's Elite 15 squad; 2023 Hyrox AG (30-34) & Overall World Champion, added a 2025 AG (35-39) title.
entries.why: The clearest window into Italy's Elite 15 push right now, with steady training and race-day content in a scene still building depth.
entries.takeaway: Post steady race-day and training content even in a scene still building depth.

entries.name: Megan Jacoby
entries.who: 2024 Hyrox World Champion and the first woman ever to break one hour; sat out the 2025 world final.
entries.why: The athlete who broke the sub-hour barrier — her return to a start line is the story to watch.
entries.takeaway: Set one hard time goal, like breaking an hour, and structure training specifically around it.

entries.name: Rich Ryan
entries.who: Founder of Reinforced Running; Elite 15 racer who ran 53:57 in Phoenix and is heading to the Stockholm World Championships.
entries.why: His breakdowns of running strategy inside a Hyrox race are some of the most concretely useful coaching content in the sport.
entries.takeaway: Work on your running strategy inside the race itself, not just station strength.

entries.name: James Newbury
entries.who: Five-time CrossFit Games athlete and CrossFit Games Team champion, former semi-pro rugby player, now racing Hyrox Elite 15 doubles.
entries.why: Podiums with Toomey in mixed doubles make him one of the clearest CrossFit-to-Hyrox pipelines to watch.
entries.takeaway: Cross-train in CrossFit-style strength and conditioning to build doubles-race durability.

entries.name: Kris Rugloski
entries.who: 2022 Hyrox World Champion and a 65-race veteran who fought back from a torn meniscus to reclaim her Elite 15 spot at the Barcelona Last Chance Qualifier.
entries.why: A comeback story with real depth — she also races ultras, having debuted at the Barkley Marathons.
entries.takeaway: Cross-train endurance events alongside Hyrox to build a deeper aerobic base.

entries.name: Eugenio Bianchi
entries.who: Italy's Hyrox Pro record holder (55:57), on the Elite 15 roster three seasons running, with a long Spartan Race podium history before switching sports.
entries.why: One of the most-followed Italian Hyrox profiles, bridging an OCR audience into the sport with regular race breakdowns.
entries.takeaway: Bring an obstacle-racing background's grip and carry strength into your Hyrox stations.

entries.name: Lukas Storath
entries.who: The first Hyrox World Champion; now CEO and founder of Athletic Camps, running online Hyrox coaching.
entries.why: One of the few voices who can talk about the sport's early days and its current programming with equal authority.
entries.takeaway: Study the sport's early history to understand why current training methods evolved this way.

entries.name: Nick Bare
entries.who: Fitness YouTuber (1.46M subscribers) whose cinematic, multi-part 'Hyrox Prep' series documented his own build toward the sport.
entries.why: Brings a massive outside fitness/military audience into Hyrox with genuinely watchable long-form content.
entries.takeaway: Document your full training build toward a race goal — filming your own prep builds accountability.

entries.name: Pelayo Menendez
entries.who: Spanish Elite 15 racer and founder of PELE Performance, back on the 2026 World Championships doubles podium a year after a ruptured Achilles.
entries.why: The leading Spanish-language voice in the sport — constant Instagram lives, podcasts, and Facebook-group coaching.
entries.takeaway: Rehab a serious injury with patience and return to racing rather than rushing back.

entries.name: Jonathon Wynn
entries.who: Australian ex-special-forces soldier and Elite 15 regular, top 10 at three straight World Championships (6th, 9th, 5th).
entries.why: A sobriety-since-2020 story layered on genuine elite results, plus he's outspoken about being passed over for Australia's relay squad.
entries.takeaway: Use structured, disciplined daily habits as the backbone of your race prep.

entries.name: Jack Driscoll
entries.who: American HYROX Elite hopeful and full-time firefighter; sub-60 Pro Solo winner (Vancouver) chasing his first Elite 15 spot.
entries.why: Follow for in-depth, reference-quality training breakdowns filmed with actual Elite 15 athletes, from a firefighter with a sub-5 mile and a 500lb squat.
entries.takeaway: Balance a strong running base with heavy strength work rather than picking one over the other.

entries.name: Kristi Eramo O'Connell
entries.who: Seven-time CrossFit Games competitor who retired from CrossFit and won her Hyrox pro debut in Houston, then took Mixed Doubles in Dallas.
entries.why: A CrossFit veteran who didn't just dabble in Hyrox — she won straight out of the gate and kept winning.
entries.takeaway: Bring proven work capacity from another sport directly into your first Hyrox races.

entries.name: Cole Learn
entries.who: Canadian Elite 15 racer, 2026 HYROX Americas Champion and Chicago Pro winner (54:36) with a public addiction-recovery story.
entries.why: Fast-rising racer whose personal story pulls readers who have never heard of HYROX before.
entries.takeaway: Use consistent race training itself as a structured recovery tool.

entries.name: Fabian Eisenlauer
entries.who: German HYROX Elite athlete and running coach; set the men's open doubles world record with Jake Williamson in 2025 and holds one of the fastest men's open times ever.
entries.why: Follow for a genuine ex-smoker-to-elite transformation story and running-coach breakdowns that double as real training content.
entries.takeaway: Build your running volume up gradually from a low baseline toward elite pace.

entries.name: Sinéad Bent
entries.who: UK physiotherapist and Elite 15 athlete who went from newcomer to elite level in a single year.
entries.why: A fast-rising British racer with a genuinely engaged following and brand deals (Gymshark, Garmin) to match.
entries.takeaway: Use knowledge of your own body's mechanics to fast-track from newcomer to elite.

entries.name: Mat Fraser
entries.who: Five-time CrossFit Games champion (2016-2020) who came out of retirement to race Hyrox doubles in New York and Las Vegas.
entries.why: The most dominant CrossFitter ever taking Hyrox seriously, on camera, is the single biggest crossover storyline the sport has right now.
entries.takeaway: Come back for select doubles events even after retirement if the format still excites you.

entries.name: Hidde Weersma
entries.who: Dutch Elite 15 racer and coach who broke the Men's Pro world record (52:42) at the 2026 EMEA Championships in London.
entries.why: First man under 53 minutes and the mind behind LO:HYROX, a data-driven training program other Elite 15 racers use.
entries.takeaway: Use data-driven pacing plans for each station instead of racing on feel alone.

entries.name: Vivian Tafuto
entries.who: Full-time actuary and Elite 15 podium regular; with Lauren Weeks holds the women's doubles world record (52:59).
entries.why: Proof a full-time job and elite Hyrox racing aren't mutually exclusive, plus a doubles world record.
entries.takeaway: Fit elite-level training around a full-time career — a demanding job doesn't rule out podiums.

entries.name: Charlie Botterill
entries.who: English Elite 15 racer and former pro cyclist, part of the second-fastest Men's Pro Doubles time ever run (48:05, Barcelona 2026).
entries.why: Quit his job to go all-in on HYROX in 2026 — a fast-rising name with a genuinely different backstory.
entries.takeaway: Go all-in on training for a season if you're serious about a breakthrough result.

entries.name: Harry Thompson
entries.who: English HYROX Elite athlete; 2025 Men's Pro World Champion (all age groups, Chicago) and member of England's bronze-medal 2026 Mixed Relay team.
entries.why: Follow for an honest, no-filter look at life as a world champion who left corporate law to race and coach full-time.
entries.takeaway: Be honest and transparent about your process, not just the highlight-reel wins.

entries.name: Lucy Procter
entries.who: 22-year-old Red Bull/Puma-backed Elite 15 racer and 2024 Hyrox U24 world champion.
entries.why: One of the youngest names in the Elite 15 and already climbing the senior world rankings.
entries.takeaway: Start racing age-group divisions young to build competitive experience before moving up to senior fields.

entries.name: Quentin Pingliez
entries.who: French coach who says he took the Mixed World and EU overall title in 2025; posts as @coach_pgz.
entries.why: A rising French voice mixing his own recent results with day-to-day coaching content.
entries.takeaway: Share your own current race results alongside your coaching content so advice stays grounded.

entries.name: Choi Seung-yeon
entries.who: 4x CrossFit Games athlete and Physical: Asia star who took 2nd in Doubles at Hyrox Singapore 2025 alongside Amotti.
entries.why: Elite CrossFit credibility plus mainstream Netflix fame makes her a strong entry point for new fans.
entries.takeaway: Bring elite conditioning from another sport directly into Hyrox doubles rather than starting from scratch.

entries.name: Tiago Lousa
entries.who: Portuguese Hyrox coach with 58 races and 55 podiums logged; runs coaching under TheLousaWay.
entries.why: Few coaches have that much race volume to draw lessons from, and he shares it openly.
entries.takeaway: Rack up race volume deliberately — dozens of starts teach patterns a few races never will.

entries.name: Amotti
entries.who: Physical: 100 Season 2 winner and Team Korea member who took 2nd in the Doubles race at AIA Hyrox Singapore 2025.
entries.why: Pulls a huge Netflix-built audience into Hyrox through upbeat training vlogs.
entries.reach: IG follower count not independently confirmed; Physical: 100-driven following (approx 2026)
entries.takeaway: Keep your training content upbeat and consistent — energy in your posts pulls in new racers.

entries.name: Marc Dean
entries.who: 2024 Pro Doubles World Champion alongside Jake Dearden, and a Hyrox coach who breaks down doubles strategy for his own athletes.
entries.why: A genuine doubles-title résumé plus a coaching voice aimed squarely at age-group doubles teams.
entries.takeaway: Study doubles-specific strategy explicitly — pairing tactics differ from solo racing and deserve separate practice.

entries.name: Rebecca Mason
entries.who: Britain's most successful female HYROX racer historically; 2022 age-group World Champion and Elite 15 competitor 2022-2024, now a full-time HYROX 1-1 coach.
entries.why: Follow for coaching grounded in real Elite 15 experience, from a former elite gymnast who built her own path in the sport.
entries.takeaway: Draw on your background in another sport to inform technique, not just raw fitness.

entries.name: Saskia Millard
entries.who: London A&E doctor who set a European Hyrox Pro record (57:26) just months into her racing career.
entries.why: A near-zero-training-time breakout in a sport that's getting more professionalized by the season — worth watching how far it goes.
entries.takeaway: Don't assume a demanding job blocks fast results — smart training on limited hours still works.

entries.name: Seena Akbary
entries.who: Dubai-based founder of Energy Camp and 2024 Hyrox Cape Town Champion, now an Under Armour Middle East athlete.
entries.why: By far the biggest following of any Hyrox figure in the Gulf, and a genuine builder of the region's scene rather than just a racer.
entries.takeaway: Build the local scene around you, not just your own results, if you want to grow the sport.

entries.name: Jade Skillen
entries.who: Hyrox performance coach sponsored by Puma and Mira Fit, the most-followed Hyrox coach on this list.
entries.why: Consistent, brand-backed training content aimed at everyday racers, not just the elite field.
entries.takeaway: Follow programming aimed at everyday racers, not just the elite field, if that's your level.

entries.name: Max Pineau
entries.who: French HYROX Pro athlete and TikTok star (posts as "pinaliste"); races doubles and solo Pro divisions while building one of the sport's biggest short-form followings.
entries.why: Follow for high-volume, high-energy running and HYROX content that pulls a huge general-fitness audience into the sport.
entries.takeaway: Post high-volume, high-energy training content consistently — frequency builds an audience as much as quality.

entries.name: Till Schenk
entries.who: Hyrox livestream co-commentator and Global Event Emcee/TV host for Hyrox and Eurosport, based in Munich; former 14-season Ironman athlete.
entries.why: His race-day commentary is the voice most fans associate with the sport's biggest broadcasts.
entries.takeaway: Bring endurance-sport background into how you pace and think through the longer stations.

entries.name: Louis Osselaer
entries.who: Belgian Elite 15 racer who went from age-group world champion to 2026 HYROX World Championships silver medalist.
entries.why: This season's breakout — the sled-pull specialist nobody was talking about until he nearly won Stockholm.
entries.takeaway: Turn a weak station into a specialty — dedicated focus on one weakness can carry you to a podium.

entries.name: Joffrey Voisin
entries.who: France's best-known Hyrox name, a four-time Masters (40+) World Champion who only started racing in his 40s.
entries.why: A late-start comeback story with French-language coaching content that doubles as the entry point for French fans discovering the sport.
entries.takeaway: Start training seriously even in your 40s if you haven't already — elite performance is still reachable.

entries.name: Noah Ohlsen
entries.who: Multi-time CrossFit Games veteran, 2019 Games runner-up and 'Spirit of the Games' award winner, who raced Hyrox Elite Doubles at the 2026 World Championships.
entries.why: One of CrossFit's most respected names lends the format his credibility and his built-in following.
entries.takeaway: Bring mental toughness and sportsmanship built in another discipline directly into your Hyrox doubles racing.

entries.name: Tomas Tvrdik
entries.who: Czech soldier and Elite 15 racer, EMEA champion in 2026 with a sub-55-minute personal best at age 40.
entries.why: No man over 40 has gone faster — a genuine outlier chasing a world title on almost no training volume.
entries.takeaway: Chase a fast pace even on low training volume by prioritizing quality sessions over total hours.

entries.name: Graham Halliday
entries.who: Scottish Elite 15 racer, widely regarded as the UK's fastest HYROX athlete, 10th at the 2025 World Championships.
entries.why: Full-time coach and gym owner whose podcast and YouTube channel teach the sport from race-day intensity down to basics.
entries.takeaway: Learn the sport from both ends — race-day intensity and the basics — not just one.

entries.name: Kyle Schoonbee
entries.who: Tokyo 2020 Olympic rower turned South African Hyrox champion, winning Men's Pro at both Cape Town and Johannesburg.
entries.why: An Olympic-caliber engine redirected at Hyrox, in a South African scene that's still young — a genuine crossover story to watch grow.
entries.takeaway: Redirect an existing endurance engine from another sport toward Hyrox instead of building fitness from zero.

entries.name: Katherine Fahsbender
entries.who: American HYROX Pro racer who went from casual runner to Pro Women's winner (Atlanta) and Pro Doubles winner (Houston) in about 18 months.
entries.why: Follow to watch one of the sport's fastest-rising talents in real time as she pushes toward Elite 15 contention.
entries.takeaway: Go from casual runner to competitive racer by committing fully for a defined stretch.

entries.name: David Wetherill
entries.who: British Paralympian (three Games in table tennis) turned Hyrox Adaptive ambassador, racing with mobility aids and helping shape the division's rules.
entries.why: The face of Hyrox Adaptive — his 2025 Worlds moment, a spontaneous cheer circle at the final wall-ball station, defined the division.
entries.takeaway: Advocate for and help shape adaptive-division rules if you compete with mobility aids.

entries.name: Gustav Cordua
entries.who: Danish Elite 15 Doubles athlete and graduate engineering student who set the Danish national Pro record (55:29) at home in Copenhagen.
entries.why: A student-athlete balancing a master's degree with Elite 15 racing, with a running doubles storyline alongside partner Sebastian Ifversen.
entries.takeaway: Balance demanding academic or work commitments with structured elite training rather than choosing one.

entries.name: Maarten Enthoven
entries.who: Dutch engineer and Elite-15-calibre athlete who broke into the all-time Pro men's rankings with a 54:58 win at Hyrox Dublin.
entries.why: Founder of Pro Hyrox Stats — the follow for data-driven breakdowns of the sport as much as for his own racing.
entries.takeaway: Track and analyze your own station splits systematically the way data-driven racers do.

entries.name: Greg Williams
entries.who: Hyrox livestream co-commentator and host of Rox Lyfe, the weekly Hyrox podcast interviewing top athletes and coaches.
entries.why: The closest thing the sport has to a reference show — deep athlete interviews every week.
entries.reach: IG count not found; weekly podcast across Spotify/Apple/Amazon (approx 2026)
entries.takeaway: Listen to in-depth athlete interviews weekly to learn training philosophy straight from top performers.

entries.name: Laura Horvath
entries.who: 2023 CrossFit Games champion and three-time Rogue Invitational winner who raced Hyrox mixed doubles with her brother Kristof at the 2026 World Championships (58:43).
entries.why: One of CrossFit's biggest current stars showing up on a Hyrox start line pulls a fresh audience toward the sport.
entries.takeaway: Race doubles with a family member or close training partner you trust completely under pressure.

entries.name: Mirjam Von Rohr
entries.who: Reigning Swiss, European, and World Functional Fitness Champion and 2024-25 CrossFit Open winner who raced Hyrox Pro Women for Switzerland, finishing 7th at the 2026 World Championships.
entries.why: A genuine multi-discipline champion — CrossFit, weightlifting, powerlifting — adding Hyrox pulls functional-fitness diehards along with her.
entries.takeaway: Build raw strength through weightlifting or powerlifting before layering Hyrox-specific conditioning on top.

entries.name: Celia Duff
entries.who: "Badass Gran" — retired doctor who took up Hyrox at 68 and became age-group world champion at 65-69 (2023) and 70-74 (2024/25), and holds the 70-74 world record.
entries.why: Proof Hyrox has no age ceiling, and a joyful presence who has pulled thousands of older adults toward the sport.
entries.reach: IG account active; follower count not confirmed in search; Women's Health and CNN coverage (2026)
entries.takeaway: It's never too late to start — begin training in your 60s or 70s if you haven't yet.

entries.name: Annie Emilsson
entries.who: Swedish national Pro record holder who broke into the sport's all-time fastest women's times just seven months after her Hyrox debut.
entries.why: One of the fastest rises anywhere in the sport right now — worth following before she's a household name.
entries.takeaway: Trust rapid early progress — a strong first few months can already put you near elite pace.

entries.name: Willy Georges
entries.who: Leading French CrossFit Games athlete and former rugby player who raced Hyrox Pro Men at the 2026 World Championships, ranking first in the sled push.
entries.why: Brings France's CrossFit following to Hyrox and shows raw strength translates directly to the sled stations.
entries.takeaway: Turn background strength from another sport into a specific station advantage through focused practice.

entries.name: Choi Min-ho
entries.who: SHINee member and actor, known as Minho, who raced Hyrox Singapore's Men's Doubles alongside Physical:100's Hong Beom-seok, finishing 2nd.
entries.why: A K-pop idol podiuming at Hyrox is the kind of mainstream press the sport cannot buy.
entries.takeaway: Actually train and compete seriously in the event rather than showing up for appearance alone.

entries.name: Rachael Wade
entries.who: Alabama-based registered dietitian and mother of two who won three straight US Pro races (Houston, Miami, Ottawa) on just 7-8 training hours a week.
entries.why: A genuinely different story than most elite content in this sport: low-volume training, real job, real kids, real wins.
entries.takeaway: Win on limited training hours a week by pairing focused sessions with sound nutrition knowledge.

entries.name: Araya A. Hargate
entries.who: Thai actress and one of Thailand's most-followed public figures, who completed her Hyrox debut in Women's Doubles at Bangkok 2026.
entries.why: Her debut pulled mainstream Thai press coverage most Hyrox racers never get — the clearest crossover moment the sport has had in Southeast Asia.
entries.takeaway: Complete the race yourself, not just attend, if you want the crossover moment to mean anything.

entries.name: Robert James
entries.who: Official Hyrox Ambassador and coach behind the Sub-60 program, built on science-backed pacing plans.
entries.why: Go to him for a structured, data-driven path to breaking sub-60, not just motivation.
entries.takeaway: Follow a structured, science-backed pacing plan toward a specific time goal instead of guessing splits.

entries.name: Hong Beom-seok
entries.who: Physical:100 season-two runner-up and former South Korean special-forces soldier and firefighter who has raced Hyrox Seoul and Hyrox Singapore, taking 2nd in doubles with SHINee's Minho.
entries.why: His military-toughness fame from Physical:100 is exactly the audience Hyrox wants watching a race.
entries.takeaway: Bring military or first-responder toughness training directly into Hyrox conditioning.

entries.name: Claire Nesbitt
entries.who: Former wine critic turned full-time coach, now a Hyrox Hong Kong ambassador representing HK at the World Championships for a fourth straight year.
entries.why: One of the only dedicated Hyrox voices building the sport specifically for Hong Kong and the wider Asia scene.
entries.takeaway: Build the local scene, not just your own results, if coaching becomes your real passion.

entries.name: Aoife O'Rourke
entries.who: Two-time Olympic boxer and 2025 World Championship boxing silver medalist from Ireland; won a HYROX doubles age-group World title with sister Lisa in 2025.
entries.why: Follow for the novelty of an Olympic-level combat-sport athlete crossing over into HYROX and bringing her boxing following with her.
entries.takeaway: Bring combat-sport conditioning, like footwork and explosive power, into your Hyrox stations.

entries.name: Calypso Sheridan
entries.who: Australian Elite 15 singles and doubles racer; with Meg Martin set the women's doubles world record (53:21) and finished top 5 at the 2026 Worlds.
entries.why: A double threat racing both the singles Elite 15 and record-setting doubles.
entries.takeaway: Race both the singles Elite 15 field and doubles events in the same season.

entries.name: Madelyn Eybergen
entries.who: Canadian university cross-country champion turned Hyrox convert — the first Canadian woman under 60 minutes and a Pro 20-24 World Champion.
entries.why: A running pedigree this deep rarely crosses into Hyrox this fast — worth watching as she moves up divisions.
entries.takeaway: Convert a running background directly into Hyrox — cross-country speed transfers well to the run stations.

entries.name: Aldo Lozano Marquez
entries.who: Mexican Hyrox ambassador on the Puma Mexico roster with 20-plus podiums racing across Mexico, Brazil, Spain, and the US.
entries.why: The face of HYROX Mexico's ambassador program — the follow for LatAm race coverage and hybrid-performance coaching.
entries.takeaway: Travel to race across different countries and circuits to build broader competitive experience faster.

entries.name: Jannik Czapla
entries.who: German HYROX Elite 15 athlete and HYROX Germany ambassador; part of Germany's silver-medal 2026 Mixed Relay team alongside Tim Wenisch and Linda Meier.
entries.why: Follow a young German elite building a coaching brand alongside his own Elite 15 racing career.
entries.takeaway: Build a coaching brand alongside your own racing career from early on, not after retiring.

entries.name: Lily Sharp
entries.who: Australian HYROX Pro Doubles athlete with results across multiple seasons and partners (national top-3 rankings); active HYROX content creator.
entries.why: Follow for a working Pro-division racer's view of the doubles circuit, from qualifiers through World Championships.
entries.takeaway: Race with different doubles partners across seasons to learn what pairing style suits you best.

entries.name: Danél Louw
entries.who: South African Hyrox Pro-division champion (Johannesburg, Cape Town) chasing an Elite 15 World Championship podium.
entries.why: The sport's clearest breakout story out of South Africa, now backed by a growing brand roster.
entries.takeaway: Build your Hyrox résumé at home first before targeting an Elite 15 world podium.

entries.name: Tobias Lautwein
entries.who: German HYROX World Champion (2021) and European Champion (2022), a former world-record holder now racing at Pro rather than Elite 15 level.
entries.why: One of the sport's earliest champions — still racing and still a name podcasts want, though he dropped out of the Elite 15 for 2025-26.
entries.takeaway: Keep racing at whatever level fits your current life, even after stepping down from the top tier.

entries.name: Nico Bolzico
entries.who: Argentine-born fitness entrepreneur and Philippine media personality who completed his Hyrox debut in Seoul in 1:16 alongside the country's fastest Hyrox Pro racer.
entries.why: A fitness-focused celebrity who trained and actually finished, not just showed up for photos.
entries.takeaway: Actually train specifically for the race, not just show up as a fitness personality.

entries.name: Maurice Andre
entries.who: Paraplegic adaptive athlete, posting as @SCImotivation, who took up Hyrox after a paragliding accident and was named Hyrox's Inspirational Athlete of the Year 2024.
entries.why: Advocacy-first content from Team Hyrox Allgäu that has opened the adaptive division to a wider audience.
entries.reach: IG account active; follower count not confirmed in search (2026)
entries.takeaway: Adapt your training to your body's real situation and share the process openly.

entries.name: Charlotte Haglund
entries.who: Swedish HYROX Pro Women athlete who ranked 13th of 731 (top 1%) at the 2025 World Championships and raced on Sweden's 2026 Elite 15 and Mixed Relay teams.
entries.why: Follow a quietly excellent Nordic racer whose results outpace her current profile.
entries.takeaway: Let quiet, consistent top-tier finishes build your credibility even without a big following.

entries.name: Jonne Koski
entries.who: Finnish CrossFit-scene veteran who teamed up with Olympic cross-country skiing champion Iivo Niskanen for a Hyrox doubles debut in Helsinki (Pro Doubles 30-34, 58:02).
entries.why: The Koski-Niskanen pairing pulled Finland's ski and CrossFit crowds into a Hyrox stream at the same time.
entries.takeaway: Pair with an athlete from a different endurance background to combine complementary strengths in doubles.

entries.name: Anne Curtis
entries.who: Filipino actress and TV host who raced Hyrox Seoul with husband Erwan Heussaff as a celebrity-couple entry.
entries.why: One of the Philippines' biggest media stars racing Hyrox brings a huge Southeast Asian audience with her.
entries.takeaway: Race Hyrox as a couple if you want a shared training goal with your partner.

entries.name: Emilie Dahmen
entries.who: Dutch Elite 15 singles racer, ranked inside the current world top 10 heading into the 2026 World Championships.
entries.why: The Netherlands' top Hyrox export, holding a steady top-10 world ranking.
entries.takeaway: Aim for a steady top-10 world ranking through consistency rather than chasing one peak race.

entries.name: Dong Hyun Kim
entries.who: Former UFC welterweight ('Stun Gun') who anchored Team South Korea to victory at the Hyrox x Stan Browney creator race.
entries.why: A legit ex-UFC fighter winning a Hyrox creator event shows the format rewards real athletic pedigree, not just influencer clout.
entries.takeaway: Bring combat-sport conditioning and mental toughness directly into team Hyrox racing.

entries.name: Sebastian Ifversen
entries.who: Danish Elite 15 racer with dozens of races across six seasons and consistent top-10 major finishes.
entries.why: A dependable Elite 15 name for readers tracking the full field, not just the podium.
entries.takeaway: Rack up race experience across many seasons — consistent finishes come from repeated starts, not one big prep.

entries.name: Agnieszka Maciejewska
entries.who: HYROX Poland ambassador with 13 gold and 4 silver national medals and a 2022 Spartan Race World Championship age-group title.
entries.why: A veteran of Poland's obstacle-racing-to-Hyrox pipeline, now coaching business and personal-effectiveness clients alongside her own racing.
entries.takeaway: Bring obstacle-racing grip and terrain skills into Hyrox if that's your athletic background.

entries.name: Seka Arning
entries.who: German Elite 15 singles racer for the 2026 World Championships in Stockholm.
entries.why: One of three Germans in the current Elite 15 women's field, evidence of the country's rising depth.
entries.takeaway: Train inside a strong national group — surrounding yourself with other elite racers raises your own level.

entries.name: Alyssa McElheny
entries.who: American Elite 15 singles racer for the 2026 World Championships in Stockholm.
entries.why: Part of the deep US contingent pushing the pace at every major.
entries.takeaway: Train inside a deep national field — pushing against strong training partners raises your pace.

entries.name: George Edwards
entries.who: Hyrox coach and athlete linked to The Hybrid Project, posting as @ge_training.
entries.why: A smaller-following coach worth a follow for straightforward, no-frills Hyrox programming.
entries.takeaway: Keep your programming simple and no-frills rather than overcomplicating training with unnecessary variety.

entries.name: Delphin Kruithof Kremer
entries.who: Hyrox ambassador, athlete, and head coach offering triathlon, running, and Hyrox programming.
entries.why: Worth following for programming that bridges endurance racing and Hyrox-specific training.
entries.takeaway: Bridge endurance-sport training, like triathlon or running, with Hyrox-specific work instead of treating them separately.

entries.name: Iivo Niskanen
entries.who: Three-time Olympic cross-country skiing champion who raced his first Hyrox doubles event in Helsinki alongside CrossFit's Jonne Koski.
entries.why: One of Finland's biggest sporting names trying the format on camera brings mainstream endurance-sport eyes to Hyrox.
entries.takeaway: Bring a lifetime aerobic base from another endurance sport straight into your first Hyrox race.

entries.name: Erwan Heussaff
entries.who: Entrepreneur and media personality who completed Hyrox Seoul as part of a celebrity-couple entry with wife Anne Curtis.
entries.why: A Philippine lifestyle-media heavyweight actually finishing Hyrox is free exposure to an audience the sport hasn't reached yet.
entries.takeaway: Finish the race yourself before promoting it — completing it earns credibility no endorsement can buy.

entries.name: Isaac Sanderson
entries.who: Canadian HYROX Pro athlete sponsored by LSKD and 1st Phorm; regular Pro-division racer across Canadian events.
entries.why: Follow for an under-the-radar Canadian racer's-eye view of the Pro circuit and sponsor-backed training content.
entries.takeaway: Race consistently across your regional circuit to build a sponsor-worthy track record over time.

entries.name: Jess Pettrow
entries.who: Australian Elite 15 singles racer, part of the country's deep women's contingent alongside Wietrzyk and Sheridan.
entries.why: A steady major-race performer with room to climb the Elite 15 ranks.
entries.takeaway: Keep showing up at major races steadily — consistent starts build the ranking climb over time.

entries.name: Renaud Boutillier
entries.who: French Hyrox coach posting training content as @renaud.hyrox.coach.
entries.why: A smaller French-language voice for athletes who want coaching content outside English-language channels.
entries.takeaway: Create training content in your own language if it reaches racers other channels miss.

entries.name: Alejandro Rojas-Marcos & Julio Paneque
entries.who: Former mayor of Sevilla, 85, and his partner Julio Paneque, 59 — combined age 144 — who won age-group doubles bronze at the 2026 Hyrox World Championships in Stockholm.
entries.why: The most-shared age-group story of the 2026 season, and a case study in no upper age limit for Hyrox doubles.
entries.reach: No social following found; Spanish and English press coverage only (2026)
entries.takeaway: Keep training and competing in doubles well into your seventies and eighties — age doesn't cap performance.

entries.name: Dexter Buchanan
entries.who: New Zealand racer, one of seven new qualifiers to the 2026 HYROX Elite 15 men's field.
entries.why: Worth watching as a first-season Elite 15 name from a country new to the sport's top tier.
entries.takeaway: Qualify for the top tier before worrying about results there — making the field is the first goal.

entries.name: Sean Noble
entries.who: Irish racer, one of seven new qualifiers to the 2026 HYROX Elite 15 men's field.
entries.why: A first-season Elite 15 name to watch as Ireland's presence in the sport's top tier grows.
entries.takeaway: Treat your first Elite 15 season as building experience, not chasing an immediate podium.

entries.name: Luke Greer
entries.who: English racer, one of seven new qualifiers to the 2026 HYROX Elite 15 men's field.
entries.why: New to the Elite 15 in 2026 and part of a deep British contingent at the top of the sport.
entries.takeaway: Push into a deep national field on purpose — tougher training partners at home raise your ceiling.

entries.name: Morgan Schulz
entries.who: American Elite 15 singles racer for the 2026 World Championships in Stockholm.
entries.why: Another deep-bench US racer keeping the field honest week to week.
entries.takeaway: Compete inside a deep bench of racers — consistent starts keep you sharp for bigger meets.

entries.name: Gabrielle Nikora-Baker
entries.who: New Zealand's Elite 15 singles racer for the 2026 World Championships.
entries.why: The only Kiwi in the current Elite 15 women's field.
entries.takeaway: Represent your country's scene even without local peers at your level — go race the world field anyway.

entries.name: Lena Putters
entries.who: Belgian Elite 15 singles racer for the 2026 World Championships.
entries.why: Belgium's flag-bearer in the world's toughest field.
entries.takeaway: Race for your country's flag even in the toughest field, and help build the depth behind you.

entries.name: Stefanie Oswald
entries.who: German Elite 15 singles racer for the 2026 World Championships in Stockholm.
entries.why: The third German name in the current Elite 15 — depth that's reshaping the leaderboard.
entries.takeaway: Contribute to your national scene's depth — one more elite name raises the whole field around it.

bubblingUnder.name: Pete Langsjoen
bubblingUnder.who: Became a Hyrox world champion in the men's 75-79 age group at 77, training out of Life Time facilities in California.
bubblingUnder.why: A lifelong-training blueprint that shows the sport scales to any age, profiled in Experience Life magazine.
bubblingUnder.reach: No social presence found; Experience Life magazine profile only (2026)
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Keep training consistently at a real facility into your seventies — routine, not age, decides your ceiling.

bubblingUnder.name: Annie Reid
bubblingUnder.who: 75-year-old breast cancer survivor from Essex who raced solo at the 2026 Hyrox World Championships in Stockholm, finishing 12th in the women's 70-74 category, and aims to be the first woman to race solo at 80.
bubblingUnder.why: One of the sport's most-covered human-interest stories, pure grit with no following required.
bubblingUnder.reach: No social presence found; BBC, Yahoo Sports and Boxrox coverage only (2026)
bubblingUnder.takeaway: Set a long-range goal and keep training toward it despite past setbacks like illness.
